results.title: Glofitamab-gxbm - NCI
results.content:
## Use in Cancer

Glofitamab-gxbm is approved to treat:

 B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) that has come back or did not get better after at least two other systemic therapies. It is used in adults with the following types of B-cell NHL:
  + diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)
  + large B-cell lymphoma in patients who had follicular lymphoma

Glofitamab-gxbm is approved under FDA’s Accelerated Approval Program. As a condition of approval, confirmatory trial(s) must show that it provides a clinical benefit in these patients.

Glofitamab-gxbm is also being studied in the treatment of other types of cancer.

## More About Glofitamab-gxbm

Definition from the NCI Drug Dictionary - Detailed scientific definition and other names for this drug. [...] # Glofitamab-gxbm

Placeholder slot

 (gloh-FIH-tah-mab)

Glofitamab-gxbm works by bringing healthy T cells (immune cells that help kill cancer cells) and lymphoma cells close together so the T cells can more effectively kill the lymphoma cells. It does this by binding to a protein called CD3 on healthy T cells and a protein called CD20 on B cells (the immune cells that are cancerous in B-cell lymphomas). Glofitamab-gxbm is a type of immunotherapy drug called a bispecific T-cell engager (BiTE).

US Brand Name(s)

Columvi

FDA Approved
